one_month_reasoning: Events in the 2026-10-01 to 2026-10-30 window: (1) Micron FQ4 results after the close on Sep 30 (guide $50B, ~86% GM; HBM3E/HBM4 booked through CY2027) set the tone for AI-memory names on Oct 1 - a strong print confirms demand but also that HBM supply and cost are the binding constraint on GPU volumes; (2) TSMC Q3 results and monthly sales mid-October; (3) Intel Q3 (late Oct) for server-CPU share read-through; (4) the Oct 27-28 FOMC after the Sep-16 25bp hike, with one more hike signalled - a real rate-sensitivity risk for a ~39x-FY27 stock; (5) hyperscaler Q3 prints and 2027 capex guides in the last week of October; (6) AMD's own Q3 report: AMD has not announced a date (IR page has no release as of Sep 30); Nov 3 is an aggregator estimate, and 2 of the last 5 Q3 reports (Oct 26 2021, Oct 29 2024) fell before Oct 30, so I put ~25-30% on it landing inside the window. With no directional edge from these (chain read-throughs have been positive, but the stock is near its $639 high after +281%), I keep a near-symmetric lognormal centred on spot with ~21% monthly sigma (slightly above annual/3.5 = 20.6%) to allow for the possible in-window earnings print and FOMC, with a hair more mass in both tails than round 1.

fair_value.method: Blend of P/E (NTM EPS at Sep-2027 ~$19.3 after ~3.9% expected dilution x 30x = $578, weight 0.6) and EV/sales (NTM revenue at Sep-2027 ~$102B x 10x + ~$9.9B net cash over ~1.723B diluted shares = $598, weight 0.4); diluted count = 1.659B + ~50M expected first-GW warrant shares + ~13.6M World Labs shares.

inputs_detail.derivation: ~38% growth on $15.58, consistent with management's >$20 target; chain evidence supports continued 2028 growth (hyperscaler 2027 capex >$1T, TSMC CoWoS sold out, Micron HBM demand extending into 2028) but HBM being fully booked through CY2027 caps upside volume for a second-source GPU vendor, so I do not go above ~$21.5.

1.659B Q2'26 diluted count. Warrants: none vested at June 27 (10-Q). Both OpenAI and Meta first tranches vest on the first 1GW shipped (shipments begin 2H26 for both). Assuming equal tranches across 6GW (~27M shares each; tranche sizes not disclosed, judgment), I put ~80% on OpenAI's first tranche and ~65% on Meta's first tranche vesting by Sep-2027 plus ~10M expected from second tranches = ~50M expected warrant shares. World Labs: $8.2B / ~$604 VWAP = ~13.6M shares, closing by year-end 2026. Total ~64M (~3.9%). Down from round-1's ~90M, which implied more than first tranches.

Stock at ~38.8x FY27 consensus and ~42x NTM; by Sep-2027 DC growth decelerates from ~100% toward 30-40%, so the multiple compresses toward high-growth semi peers; Nvidia (75% GM) is the ceiling comparable. Each 1x = ~$19/share.

bear.story: AI-capex digestion in 2027 (hyperscalers debt-funding capex per FactSet), Helios ramp pace disappoints (rack integration, HBM4 allocation going to Nvidia first while memory is booked through 2027), memory costs squeeze GPU margins and PC units fall 10-20%; FY27 EPS ~$13-14, warrants mostly unvested, ~23x NTM.

base.story: Helios ships from late Q3 2026 with step-ups in Q4 and Q1'27; first GW for OpenAI and Meta, Anthropic from 1H27; DC roughly doubles in 2027 and FY27 EPS lands near $15.6; EPYC keeps taking server share (Mercury 46% vs Xeon SP); NTM EPS ~$19.3 after ~4% dilution at ~31-32x.

bull.story: Compute scarcity persists across the chain (TSMC CoWoS sold out, Micron HBM booked into 2028, Intel/Nvidia supply-limited), AMD becomes a clear second GPU source with >$25 NTM EPS and the market holds ~38-40x.

thesis_break_reason: Below ~$360 (-40%, ~23x FY27 consensus $15.58, ~19x my diluted NTM $19.3) the stock would be pricing a real Helios/MI450 ramp slip beyond Q1'27, a cut to the OpenAI/Meta/Anthropic first-GW commitments, or a hyperscaler 2027 capex reset - i.e. FY27 EPS back toward $12-13. I keep $360 rather than the supervisor's $400: with 72% realized vol and ~0.55 forward sigma, a 34% drawdown to $400 is well within one annual standard deviation and has happened repeatedly in AMD's history without a thesis change; $360 is closer to my bear-case fundamentals ($330).

reasoning: Round 2 keeps my industry-lane read and corrects the facts the supervisor established. Chain evidence still says AI compute demand exceeds supply: Nvidia guided FQ3 to $108B, TSMC raised 2026 growth to >40% with CoWoS sold out, Intel says Xeon demand outpaces supply, Mercury shows AMD at ~46% of Xeon SP+EPYC revenue, and Micron (reporting tonight) says HBM3E/HBM4 are fully booked through CY2027 with ~$100B of take-or-pay contracts. That last point cuts both ways: it confirms demand but makes memory the binding constraint and a cost headwind for a second-source GPU vendor, which is why I keep FY28 EPS at ~$21.5 rather than higher. Corrections: (a) consensus FY27 EPS is $15.58 and FY27 revenue $88.1B, so I raised my 2027 revenue from $78B and moved to an explicit NTM EPS of 0.25x$15.58+0.75x$21.5 = ~$20 before dilution; (b) share count now 1.723B: explicit first-GW tranches for OpenAI (~80%) and Meta (~65%) under an equal-tranche assumption (~27M each), plus ~10M from later tranches and the ~13.6M World Labs shares I had missed, down from 1.75B; (c) Q3 date is unconfirmed and the Oct 27-28 FOMC is in window. Net effect: fair value $580 -> $585 (P/E $578, EV/sales $598), still about 3% below spot. Scenarios 25/50/25 at $330/$610/$1000 give a mean ~$638 and a median near spot. I map this to a lognormal with median ~$600 and sigma ~0.55 (below 72% realized, which is inflated by the rerating year), with a slightly fatter left tail at $242-302; P(>=604) ~0.50. The ladder moves up by ~0.5pp near the money versus round 1. I agree with the supervisor on dilution and consensus but keep my own thesis break at $360 (see reason). Research this round was limited to 5 searches/fetches.
